title: Synthetic live replay | Canonical differential equations and the massless one-loop box
scope: Live-search demonstration assessing only the three public, illustrative claims in the request. The search covers public theoretical high-energy physics literature from early differential-equation methods through 2026-10-08, focusing on canonical master-integral bases, epsilon expansions as iterated integrals, and the massless one-loop on-shell box family. The requester has no public manuscript. This report assesses current novelty at the assessment date, not the requester's historical public priority. It does not assess a real unpublished project.
summary: Synthetic live-search example — substantially scooped: Henn's 2013 arXiv v1 already presented the general strategy of choosing a master-integral basis to obtain an epsilon-factorized canonical form and solve it through iterated integrals. The 2014 lecture notes v1 gave the same type of constant-matrix equation and order-by-order integration for the massless one-loop box family.
recommendation: Do not publish this general solution strategy or the massless one-loop box demonstration as a new method. Position it as a teaching exposition with prior-work citations, or first add an independently meaningful new algorithm, proof of applicability, treatment beyond polylogarithms, or complete result for a specific new topology.

claims.text: Choose a Feynman master-integral basis so that the dimensionally regulated differential equations take the form d f = epsilon (sum_i A_i d log W_i) f, with constant matrices A_i, and present this as a general solution strategy.
claims.reason: Henn 2013 v1 already proposed choosing a preferred master-integral basis to obtain an epsilon-factorized canonical form. Its general equation and two-loop example give d f = epsilon dA f and a system of constant matrices multiplying dlog letters, respectively. The user proposes no additional algorithm, proof, or broader applicability that would establish a material distinction.

claims.text: Expand the canonical equations in epsilon and obtain iterated-integral solutions from a path-ordered exponential or order-by-order integration.
claims.reason: Henn 2013 v1 already expresses the canonical solution as a path-ordered exponential and explicitly states that the perturbative epsilon solution consists of iterated integrals. The 2014 v1 notes also give the general Chen iterated-integral solution and its order-by-order expansion.

claims.text: Use the massless one-loop on-shell box family to demonstrate the basis choice, canonical form, and order-by-order integration in epsilon.
claims.reason: The teaching example in Henn 2014 v1 is exactly the massless one-loop 2-to-2 box family: it gives a basis, obtains the constant-matrix system epsilon[a/x+b/(1+x)], and integrates order by order in epsilon. The earlier 1992 work also uses differential equations for the dimensionally regulated massless one-loop box integral.

sources.title: Multiloop integrals in dimensional regularization made simple
sources.version: arXiv:1304.1806v1 (v1 checked directly; current-version content was not backdated to v1)
sources.locator: PDF page 2 (one-based), Eqs. (4), (6), (7); PDF page 3, Eqs. (17), (18) and the following discussion of the alphabet and order-by-order solution
sources.finding: The paper proposes obtaining epsilon-factorized differential equations through a preferred master-integral basis, writes the path-ordered exponential solution, and states that its epsilon expansion consists of iterated integrals. The massless two-loop 2-to-2 example gives a constant-coefficient system with dlog letters x and 1+x.
sources.difference: Its worked example is at two loops rather than the proposed one-loop box, but that distinction does not preserve novelty for the central general method or solution steps.

sources.title: Lectures on differential equations for Feynman integrals
sources.locator: Printed pages 10–11 (one-based PDF pages 11–12), Eqs. (3.14)–(3.20): massless one-loop 2-to-2 box family; printed page 17 (PDF page 18), Eqs. (5.1)–(5.4): general canonical form and Chen iterated-integral solution
sources.finding: The notes choose a three-element basis for the massless one-loop on-shell box family and obtain ∂x g = epsilon[a/x+b/(1+x)]g with constant matrices a and b. They then set g=sum_k epsilon^k g^(k) and integrate order by order. They also express the general multivariable solution as Chen iterated integrals.
sources.difference: There is no material difference from the proposed one-loop box demonstration and general solution procedure. This is a teaching exposition of the existing method, not merely a candidate with neighboring terminology.

sources.title: Dimensionally Regulated One-Loop Integrals
sources.locator: Title and abstract page (one-based PDF page 1); printed pages 8–9 (PDF pages 9–10), Eqs. (41)–(43) and their application discussion
sources.finding: The paper establishes differential relations for one-loop scalar integrals in D=4-2epsilon and explicitly states that the differential equations for box integrals with massless internal lines are easy to solve.
sources.difference: It does not provide the later Henn-style canonical basis and constant-matrix dlog form, so it cannot alone cover C1/C2. It establishes that the massless one-loop box was already used as a differential-equation example.

next_steps: Stop presenting C1/C2 as a first new method; cite Henn 2013 as direct prior work in any manuscript.
If the one-loop box material is retained, position it as a teaching example and cite Henn 2014 and earlier differential-equation literature on one-loop integrals.

Claim methodological innovation only after adding a verifiable technical increment, such as a new canonicalization algorithm with rigorous applicability conditions, a computable extension to non-polylogarithmic function spaces, or a complete integral result for a previously unknown topology. Search again for that precise increment.
